'''Gregor Hagedorn''' (born 1965) is a German [[botanist]] and academic director at the [[Natural History Museum, Berlin]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gregor Hagedorn {{!}} Blätter für deutsche und internationale Politik|url=https://www.blaetter.de/autoren/gregor-hagedorn|access-date=12 June 2020|website=www.blaetter.de}}</ref> {{botanist|Hagedorn|border=0}}

== Life ==

Gregor Hagedorn studied biology at the [[University of Tübingen]] and at [[Duke University]] (North Carolina).<ref name="globalgoals-forum.org">{{Cite web|title=Speaker profile – Dr. Gregor Hagedorn – Global Goals Forum|url=https://www.globalgoals-forum.org/home-en/speakers/speaker-profile-dr-gregor-hagedorn/?lang=en|access-date=12 June 2020|language=en-US|archive-date=12 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612220418/https://www.globalgoals-forum.org/home-en/speakers/speaker-profile-dr-gregor-hagedorn/?lang=en}}</ref> Afterwards, he worked in the Department of Mycology at the [[University of Bayreuth]] until 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Abteilung Mykologie: Mitarbeiter: Gregor Hagedorn|url=http://www.mycology.uni-bayreuth.de/mycology/de/mitarbeiter/mit/mitarbeiter_detail.php?id_obj=53808|access-date=14 June 2020|website=www.mycology.uni-bayreuth.de}}</ref> In 2007 his dissertation on "Structuring Descriptive Data of Organisms – Requirement Analysis and Information Models"was completed at the University of Bayreuth with [[Gerhard Rambold]] as supervisor.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Structuring Descriptive Data of Organisms — Requirement Analysis and Information Models|url=https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/632/|date=2007|place=Bayreuth|degree=Doctoral thesis|language=de|first=Gregor|last=Hagedorn}}</ref>

From 1992 to 2013 he was a staff member at the Federal Biological Research Centre for Agriculture and Forestry, now [[Julius Kühn-Institut|Julius Kühn Institute]].<ref name="globalgoals-forum.org"/> He played a major role in the development of a data standard for describing gender within the [[Biodiversity Information Standards|Taxonomic Databases Working Group]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=TDWG Membership 2004|url=https://archive.bgbm.org/TDWG/membership.htm|website=Taxonomic Databases Working Group}}</ref>

Since 2013, Hagedorn has been working at the [[Natural History Museum, Berlin|Museum of Natural History Berlin]], first as Head of Digital World and Information Science (until 2016), then as Academic Director.<ref>{{Cite news|last=WELT|date=15 March 2019|title=Schulstreiks fürs Klima: Mehr Erwachsene schließen sich an|work=DIE WELT|url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/berlin/article190338027/Schulstreiks-fuers-Klima-Mehr-Erwachsene-schliessen-sich-an.html|access-date=12 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Gregor Hagedorn {{!}} Museum für Naturkunde|url=https://www.museumfuernaturkunde.berlin/de/taxonomy/term/234/gregor.hagedorn|access-date=12 June 2020|website=www.museumfuernaturkunde.berlin}}</ref>

Between 2014 and 2018 Hagedorn was a member of the German National Council for Information Infrastructures as a representative of the scientific organisations.

== Scientists for Future ==

[[File:Scientists for Future 2019-03-12 group photograph 02 (cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Detlev Ganten]], [[Eckart von Hirschhausen]], [[Maja Göpel]], Gregor Hagedorn, [[Karen Helen Wiltshire]] and [[Volker Quaschning]] (from left to right) at the presentation of the ''#Scientists4Future'' statement on 12{{nbsp}}March 2019 in Berlin before the [[Bundespressekonferenz|Federal Press Conference]]]]

Together with other scientists, Hagedorn founded the grassroots movement [[Scientists for Future]] (S4F) in March 2019.<ref name="ronzheimer-2019" /><ref name="roloff-2021" /><ref name="fopp-etal-2021" />  This initiative was inspired by a group of Belgian scientists who had earlier offered their support to the nascent [[School strike for climate|Fridays for Future]] movement in January 2019 under the banner of Scientists for Climate.<ref name="scientists-for-climate-pdf-2020" /><ref name="scientists-for-climate-web-2020" /><ref name="hagedorn-etal-gaia-2019" />  The first statement by Scientists For Future was written by a circle of 30{{nbsp}}people and signed by 26,800 scientists in Germany, Switzerland, and Austria.<ref name="hagedorn-etal-gaia-2019" />  The key authors also published a similar statement in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' with scientists from the United States, including [[Michael Mann]] and [[Katharine Hayhoe]].<ref name="hagedorn-etal-science-2019" />  Hagedorn represented Scientists for Future at an environmental meeting with the German Federal President [[Frank-Walter Steinmeier]] in early 2020.<ref name="bundesarchiv-2020" />  In late{{nbhyph}}2021, Hagedorn presented a TEDx talk in Potsdam on the topic of sustainability.<ref name="hagedorn-2021">

== Awards ==

* 2016: Badge of Honour by the German Phytomedical Society for his commitment to create a phytomedical wiki for phytomedical terms and definitions{{nnbsp}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ehrennadel: DPG e.V.|url=https://plant-protection.net/en/die-dpg/auszeichnungen/ehrennadel|access-date=12 June 2020|website=plant-protection.net}}</ref>
* 2019: Best Paper Award from GAIA Verlag for the publication The concerns of the young protesters are justified. A statement by Scientists for Future{{nnbsp}}<ref>{{Cite web|last=www.oekom.de|first=oekom verlag GmbH-|title=Best Paper Award {{!}} Publikationen {{!}} oekom verlag|url=https://www.oekom.de/publikationen-zeitschriften/best-paper-award/c-132|access-date=12 June 2020|website=www.oekom.de|language=de}}</ref>
* 2019: Federal Sustainability Prize in the Politics category of the German Sustainability Association for Hagedorn and the Scientists For Future{{nnbsp}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bundespreis Nachhaltigkeit|url=https://nachhaltigkeit.bvng.org/bundespreis-nachhaltigkeit/|access-date=12 June 2020|website=Bundesvereinigung Nachhaltigkeit|language=de-DE}}</ref>
